correctness.rationale: Counting diagonal deletion outputs yields p+r≤2q and p≤q; counting offdiagonal outputs yields r+3d≤2q(q−1). Therefore 3|C|≤2q²+3q and |C|≤q+floor(2q²/3). For each block in a resolvable Steiner triple system the four-word ordinary or six-word parallel template covers each ordered offdiagonal pair exactly twice; selected parallel blocks cover all diagonals once and constant codewords supply their second coverage. B=q(q−1)/6 and q/3 parallel blocks give exactly q+2q²/3 distinct codewords. Classical Kirkman existence holds at all q≡3 mod6, q≥3. Equality forces p=r=q and all nonconstant repeated letters adjacent. The packaged verifier independently checks all q=3,9 output multiplicities, no extrapolation.

value.rationale: The minimum nontrivial word length for deletion-list decoding is a natural finite channel benchmark with alphabet size variable. The theorem gives an infinite sharp congruence class, an exact double-cover combinatorial construction, and structural necessary conditions on every extremizer. The preceding general converse has a quadratic gap in these parameters; the improvement and construction are mathematically substantive rather than routine parameter substitution or a finite sample.
